note.p: Godwin mentions Sir Robert Ainslie as a Truchement at John Paradise’s, which is a French word widely used in England at the time meaning interpreter. There is also a Sir Robert Ainslie mentioned in the DNB 1730-1812 as British ambassador to Constantinople (1776-1792). John Paradise was familiar with that part of the world and its languages; so it is likely to be the Sir R A as mentioned in the DNB. There is also a Sir Robert Ainslie who was listed to have a subscription for erecting a statue in honour of the previous Prime Minister, William Pitt, on May 8th, 1802. It is unclear whether this is the same Sir Robert Ainslie that Godwin mentions. Sir Robert Ainslie’s will is dated the 5 August 1812. Sir Rober Ainslie was residing in Manchester Square, Middlesex when he died.
